candidates.title: Probing Transformer Representations Layer by Layer, Module by Module
candidates.content: Which representation should be probed in a transformer-based foundation model? Recent work shows that the standard practice of probing the final layer is often suboptimal, as intermediate layers can provide better features. Yet, representations are still largely studied along depth alone, treating each transformer block as an atomic unit. In this work, we analyze transformer representations layer by layer, module by module. Through more than 144,000 linear probing evaluations of vision foundation models (VFMs) and large language models (LLMs), we show that layer and module choices should be considered jointly: the best layer-module pair yields substantially larger gains over the final-layer residual stream than the best layer with the residual stream fixed. Moreover, module performance can vary substantially across layers, showing that useful representations cannot be characterized by depth alone. Building on these findings, we evaluate simple fixed probing strategies: the final-layer feedforward activation (Act@100) for vision and the second normalization layer at 60% depth (LN2@60) for language. candidates.title: CARTBench: Rubric-Based Evaluation of Shopping Advice for Complex and Ambiguous Requests with Timelines
candidates.content: Large language model (LLM) shopping assistants now recommend products in multi-turn conversations. However, reliable evaluation faces Data scarcity and Difficulty Standardizing Criteria. To address these obstacles, we introduce CARTBench for CART (Complex and Ambiguous Requests with Timelines). For Data scarcity, we curate cases from real commercial shopping needs across 17 retail domains, pairing timestamped dialogue with 1,603 product records. For Difficulty Standardizing Criteria, we develop case-specific rubrics guided by Ideal Response Principles, distilled from excellent replies manually selected from successfully completed orders. These principles also guide Principle-Guided CART Prompting, our structured recommendation strategy. The experimental benchmark contains 1,328 expert-annotated criteria across Core, Excellence, and Safety. To answer the CART question, we evaluate 7 flagship commercial API models, including GPT-6.1-Sol and Claude-Opus-5, and 35B+ parameters open-weight models. candidates.title: Precision on Demand: Escalating Weight Bits at Uncertain Decoding Steps in a Small Local Model
candidates.content: Local decoding usually fixes one weight precision for the whole generation. We study a different allocation: store 8-bit weights, decode with their top 4 bits, and redo a step at 8 bits only when the low-precision output distribution looks uncertain (entropy above a threshold or a small top-two margin). Quantization is simulated, the model is Qwen3-0.6B, and the benchmark is GSM8K. Cost is counted in weight bytes read per token. On 36724 replayed steps the entropy of the low pass ranks argmax flips with AUC 0.93. At a 15% escalation budget it catches 78% of flips and the margin gate 94%, against the 15% expected for a random gate of equal rate (a computed expectation, not a run). In 150 live problems all-high scores 64.0% and all-low 55.3% (McNemar p=0.053). An entropy gate with a 16% escalation rate scores 62.7% at 0.87 of the all-high weight bytes. Its paired difference is -1.3 (-8.0 to +5.3) points to all-high and +7.3 (+0.0 to +14.7) points to all-low (p=0.080), so the live data do not separate the gate from either end. candidates.title: Hide your slop PR descriptions behind <details><summary>
candidates.content: Most of the changes I make to my projects these days come in the form of PRs opened for me by Claude Code or Codex. The PR is my unit of work - I use them to bundle commits together, iterating on them until a feature is complete, document decisions and then merge the finished result. Today's coding agents are great at writing PR descriptions. They're too good at describing the work The problem is that they are too good. An agent-written PR description is accurate and comprehensive. It describes the problem, the detailed solution, and the steps taken to verify it. That's a lot of information to absorb. It's not necessarily slop, but it reads like slop! It's very easy to spot an AI-written PR, and as with other forms of AI writing my instant reaction is best summarized as "I'm not reading all of that". It doesn't matter how accurate or useful the information is, I'm instantly put off by the thought that it will take me longer to read than it took the driving author to write... even when that driving author is me! candidates.title: Bipartite DNA-binding domain of transcription factor BCL11B binds clustered short DNA sequence motifs
candidates.content: Abstract B-cell leukemia/lymphoma 11B (BCL11B), despite its name, is a key regulator of T-cell development, lineage specification, and T-cell malignancies. BCL11B contains a bipartite DNA-binding domain composed of two C2H2 zinc finger arrays: low-affinity ZF2-3 and high-affinity ZF4-6. These arrays recognize similar six-nucleotide motifs, TG( n )CC( n ), as seven of the eight DNA base-contacting residues are conserved between them. The most conserved interactions involve the central GG dinucleotides, recognized by arginine and lysine residues at the key base-interacting positions of ZF3 and ZF5. We determined eight crystal structures of ZF2-3 bound to 12- or 20-base pair DNA duplexes containing either one or two binding motifs. The structures reveal that ZF2-3 recognizes DNA with remarkable configurational flexibility, binding motifs on either the same or opposite DNA strands with variable spacing in three relative orientations: head-to-tail (or tail-to-head), head-to-head, and tail-to-tail. candidates.title: Strand-displacement amplification reduces structure-induced PCR bias and preserves structurally diverse aptamers during SELEX
candidates.content: Abstract Stable secondary structures are important for aptamer folding and target recognition, but they can introduce structure-dependent amplification bias during Systematic Evolution of Ligands by Exponential Enrichment (SELEX), with G-quadruplexes (G4s) representing the most demanding case. Here, we introduce strand-displacement SELEX (SD-SELEX), which employs a polymerase with robust 5′→3′ strand-displacement activity to improve the amplification of structured templates. Comparative analyses showed that SD polymerase efficiently amplified hairpin- and G4-forming templates, whereas Taq polymerase exhibited structure-dependent amplification variability. In parallel thrombin SELEX experiments, SD-SELEX achieved 37-fold greater structural preservation and 65-fold higher batch-to-batch reproducibility than Taq-SELEX over 11 rounds. High-throughput sequencing further showed that SD-SELEX maintained G4 motif representation and progressively enriched the known 15-mer thrombin-binding aptamer through round 8, after which it was gradually replaced by newly identified G4 variants, whereas Taq-SELEX progressively depleted these sequences. candidates.title: Microfluidic concatemer sequencing unveils cooperative and competitive enhancer clusters in gene regulation
candidates.content: Abstract Chromatin looping plays a pivotal role in eukaryotic gene regulation; however, technical limitations have hindered the comprehensive characterization of higher-order interactions among genomic loci. As a result, key questions, such as whether enhancers function cooperatively or competitively at the single-molecule and ensemble levels, remain largely unresolved. Here, we present Drop-t, a novel microfluidics-based method that enables systematic profiling of higher-order chromatin architecture at both the single-molecule and population scales. We demonstrate that Drop-t is not only resistant to common ligation-induced DNA entanglements, which frequently cause nanopore clogging, but also provides greater relevance for elucidating regulatory mechanisms compared to existing ligation-free approaches. Using Drop-t, we uncovered extensive, previously underappreciated non-specific enhancer–promoter interactions (EPIs) and showed that these may influence transcriptional variability by competing with specific EPIs. Lieber and colleagues’ comment highlights the importance of distinguishing evidence for prevention from evidence for treatment. We agree with them that tranexamic acid is a life-saving treatment for postpartum haemorrhage and should be given promptly after diagnosis. The WOMAN trial showed that early tranexamic acid use for the treatment of postpartum haemorrhage is useful.1 This evidence for treatment, however, should not be interpreted as evidence for prevention, nor be used as the basis for recommending universal prophylaxis in high-burden countries.

candidates.content: SmartTrade Technologies SAS (smartTrade), a global leader in multi-asset electronic trading and payments solutions, today announced that it has acquired Celoxica, a specialist provider of ultra-low latency execution infrastructure for listed Equities, Futures, Fixed Income, and Options. Celoxica is now part of the smartTrade Group.

candidates.title: AviaGames partners Visa for player payouts
candidates.content: AviaGames, a leader in casual, skill-based mobile games, is collaborating with Visa, a world leader in digital payments, and Global Payments®, a leading payment technology and software company, to give eligible U.S. players the ability to receive payouts from Avia’s mobile games directly to their eligible Visa cards.

candidates.title: Uber adds Revolut Pay option
candidates.content: Revolut, the global bank with over 80 million customers and 850,000 business clients, today announced a milestone payments partnership expansion with Uber, the world’s leading ride-hailing and delivery platform operating in 75 countries and serving over 215 million monthly active platform consumers across the world.

candidates.title: DTCC tokenisation service to connect with Solana
candidates.content: The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), the premier post-trade market infrastructure for the global financial services industry, today announced plans to enable the tokenization of eligible The Depository Trust Company (DTC)-custodied assets on Solana.

candidates.title: Payment Options picks Tribe to power acquiring across Apac and Cema
candidates.content: Payment Options, a Singapore-headquartered Payment Service Provider, has partnered with Tribe Payments, a global issuer and acquirer processor, to provide payment processing technology and connectivity for its Acquiring business.

candidates.title: Wolters Kluwer streamlines lending for community banks and credit unions
candidates.content: Wolters Kluwer Financial & Corporate Compliance today announced the launch of ComplianceOne Plus, a cloud-based platform designed specifically for commercial and consumer lending at community banks and credit unions.

candidates.title: Nebius tests the neocloud playbook with $40 billion in planned spending
candidates.content: Nebius plans to fund its $40 billion AI infrastructure expansion through customer prepayments and loans, even as delays at a Microsoft data center raise questions about its financing model.

candidates.title: Merchants sue feds over Illinois card fee law
candidates.content: Trade groups filed lawsuits against bank and credit union regulators over a preemption of a state law that bans swipe fees for taxes and tips.

candidates.title: Uber’s UK banking partner Griffin raises $20M for stablecoin services
candidates.content: The Series B valued Griffin at more than $100 million and will help fund stablecoin reserve services and onchain cross-border payments.

candidates.title: Google and Samsung Target Holiday Shoppers With $395 AI Smart Glasses
candidates.content: Google and Samsung are targeting the holiday shopping season with nine styles of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered smart glasses starting at $395, with devices featuring Google’s Gemini assistant that will begin shipping Dec. 10. candidates.title: Fiserv preps debit network sale
candidates.content: The processing giant is shifting customers to one of its debit networks in anticipation of selling or shuttering a second one, the company’s CEO said Tuesday.
